Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage is dominated by a sharp selloff in AI-linked stocks following weak earnings signals from Alphabet and Amazon, alongside the fallout from a record $6.3 billion hack at crypto exchange Binance blamed on North Korea. Outlets are also tracking geopolitical risk to oil and shipping in the Middle East, China's economic slowdown and policy response, and how financial markets are bracing for pivotal US midterm elections.

stories.headline: AI Trade Jitters Trigger Sharp Tech Stock Selloff
stories.summary: Investors grew anxious about whether massive AI infrastructure spending is generating adequate returns, sending AI-linked shares toward bear-market territory even as the broader S&P 500 held up thanks to rotation into non-AI stocks.

stories.headline: Binance Works to Recover From Record $6.3 Billion Crypto Heist
stories.summary: Binance resumed phased withdrawals and said it had restored backing for about 90% of assets stolen in the hack, as the FBI confirmed North Korea was responsible for the theft, the largest in crypto history.

stories.headline: Alphabet's Worst Trading Day Raises Questions About Google Search's Future Value
stories.summary: Alphabet shares suffered their worst day since going public, wiping out roughly $482 billion in market value, after Bank of America cut its valuation of Google's core search business below that of fossil-fuel stocks amid AI-driven disruption to ad revenue.

stories.headline: China's Economic Slowdown Prompts Beijing to Rally Markets and Bankers
stories.summary: China's economic activity lost steam sharply in October, prompting Beijing to convene a meeting with its central bank and securities regulator on supporting the stock market and send top regulators to address global bankers in Hong Kong.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Climb as Middle East Tensions Threaten Shipping Lanes
stories.summary: Oil prices rose as an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi claims stoked supply fears, with reports that a Pakistani LNG carrier hit near Hormuz had actually secured prior Iranian approval for safe passage; OPEC+ delegates signaled the group will keep output quotas steady for December despite the turmoil.

stories.headline: Investors Brace for 'Most Consequential' US Midterms in Years
stories.summary: Big bond fund managers are pausing major portfolio moves ahead of the midterm elections and looming economic data, while prediction markets' recent record of being upset by long-shot outcomes raises doubts about their reliability this cycle.

stories.headline: Wall Street Tightens Terms as AI Build-Out Enters Costlier Phase
stories.summary: Lenders and investors are demanding stricter terms for AI infrastructure financing as cheap money dries up, while some investors are separately racing to buy insurance against the AI trade and a major hedge fund was forced to offload $800 million in debt after losses deepened.

Business.gaps: No recent business-relevant items found via search for The Information or Puck, and no distinct Business Insider feed items were provided.

US politics.overview: With midterm Election Day two days away (Tuesday, Nov. 3), nearly every outlet in this group is laser-focused on final battleground dynamics: control of the House and Senate, Trump's late-stage Justice Department interventions in disputed races, and intra-Democratic feuding in Michigan. A secondary thread covers Trump-related litigation (the dismissed WSJ defamation suit, the arch construction fight) and Supreme Court arguments beginning the November term.

stories.headline: Trump's DOJ barrels into midterms with lawsuits, raids and arrests
stories.summary: Axios details an aggressive pre-election DOJ campaign including a lawsuit to potentially delay certification of Alaska's Senate race, a suit over California noncitizen ballots, and investigations touching Rep. Ilhan Omar and Fed governor Lisa Cook; Stateline separately reports on escalating federal subpoenas to election officials.

stories.headline: House Republicans brace for midterm blowout
stories.summary: Punchbowl reports Speaker Mike Johnson is publicly bullish but GOP lawmakers privately fear a sweeping loss of their narrow House majority, with Democrats expanding the map into deep-red districts; The Hill and Roll Call also published final race-rating rundowns showing dozens of contests shifting toward Democrats.

stories.headline: El-Sayed and Stevens feud reignites days before Michigan Senate vote
stories.summary: Politico reports Democrats worry a public blowup between Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed and former rival Haley Stevens could jeopardize the party's hold on the seat; The Hill, RealClearPolitics and National Review are also covering the dispute, including a Clyburn adviser's push to keep Stevens at a planned unity event.

stories.headline: Judge dismisses Trump's $10 billion suit against Wall Street Journal
stories.summary: A federal judge threw out Trump's defamation suit against the Journal and Rupert Murdoch over an Epstein birthday-note story, calling the president's case "grasping at straws"; NYT also covered the ruling, noting it was Trump's second attempt to prove the outlet acted with actual malice.

stories.headline: Alaska 'Decoy Dan' Senate race scheme probed by DOJ
stories.summary: Coverage centers on allegations that Democratic operatives recruited a same-named candidate to confuse voters in Alaska's tight Senate race, prompting a state investigation and a DOJ lawsuit seeking to delay certification if the GOP incumbent loses; Fox News also covered the legal precedent angle.

stories.headline: Supreme Court hears religious-freedom case on Catholic pre-K program
stories.summary: The Court is weighing whether Denver's Catholic Archdiocese can exclude LGBTQ families from a state-funded universal pre-K program, part of a broader November argument session SCOTUSblog previewed, which also includes habeas and border-wall-related disputes.

stories.headline: Virginia and D.C. sue to block Trump arch construction
stories.summary: A federal judge ordered both sides to negotiate a briefing schedule after Virginia and D.C. filed suit seeking a restraining order against construction of a Trump-commissioned arch.

stories.headline: AI data centers become flashpoint in dozens of midterm races
stories.summary: Axios reports voters in 10 states face 41 data-center ballot measures Tuesday amid a bipartisan backlash, with candidates in Texas, Ohio and Utah forced to take positions after Trump praised the industry at odds with local anger.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS and Cook Political Report had no distinct recent coverage surfaced in search; Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian entries are drawn only from the provided feed items since these outlets block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Tech and AI coverage over the past day centers on cracks appearing in the AI investment boom: OpenAI's funding round falling short of target, hyperscaler debt-default insurance spiking, and Anthropic racing toward a record IPO amid credit-rating worries. Data-center backlash is also emerging as a political flashpoint in US elections, while security incidents (a backdoored Anthropic extension, OpenAI's training-data policy reversal) and Microsoft's mass voluntary-severance offer round out a day dominated by AI-industry stress signals.

stories.headline: OpenAI lowers funding round target, raising just a fraction of its goal
stories.summary: OpenAI raised only about $11 billion in its latest funding round, well short of the $30 billion target, with its valuation also falling below expectations as big investors cool on the AI trade.

stories.headline: Cost of insuring hyperscaler debt hits highest level since 2021
stories.summary: The cost of insuring against debt defaults at Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle has surged to its highest level since 2021, reflecting investor anxiety over the scale of AI infrastructure spending.

stories.headline: Anthropic nears mega-IPO as credit agencies signal 'junk' rating risk
stories.summary: Anthropic is expected to receive a high junk rating from credit agencies after its IPO, according to an FT report citing anchor investor Blackstone, a reversal from earlier expectations of an investment-grade rating; Anthropic is targeting a Nasdaq listing as soon as mid-November in what could be one of the largest IPOs in history.

stories.headline: Data centers emerge as a midterm election flashpoint
stories.summary: At a Brooklyn midterm campaign event, conversations repeatedly turned to AI data centers, underscoring how the issue has become politically salient even outside traditional tech-policy circles.

stories.headline: Binance says it will resume withdrawals after covering 95% of $6.3B hack losses
stories.summary: Binance plans to resume withdrawals in phases starting Sunday after covering roughly 95% of the approximately $6.3 billion in crypto stolen in the record-breaking hack.

stories.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary severance to a quarter of its workforce
stories.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary severance packages to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, while shielding AI-critical teams, marking its second such program this year.

stories.headline: Anthropic's VS Code extension on Cursor was backdoored for nearly 12 hours
stories.summary: A verified Anthropic account on Cursor was compromised, allowing a backdoored version of its VS Code extension to remain live for nearly 12 hours, with the attack vector still unknown.

stories.headline: OpenAI to begin training on previously off-limits cybersecurity session data
stories.summary: Starting November 29, OpenAI will use data from Daybreak Blue cybersecurity sessions to train its models even when users had opted out, prompting backlash and a follow-up promise of a separate opt-out mechanism.

Tech & AI.gaps: Platformer, MIT Technology Review, VentureBeat, Rest of World, IEEE Spectrum, NYT, FT, The Economist, and The Guardian had no distinct AI/tech lead stories from the last 24-48 hours beyond what's reflected above (several outlets, including The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist and The Guardian, could only be checked via provided feed items since they block web search).

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by fallout from the Strait of Hormuz tanker attack and related oil-market jitters, alongside corporate earnings signals from utilities (Xcel, Edison International, Hitachi) and a European gas-storage shortfall as winter approaches. Nuclear power milestones and US clean-energy policy fights (wildfire reform, renewables permitting) round out the coverage.

stories.headline: Tanker attack near Strait of Hormuz fuels oil supply fears
stories.summary: Oil prices climbed as markets worried about wider Middle East escalation following an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi claims of further strikes; Bloomberg separately reported the attacked Pakistani LNG carrier had secured prior safe-passage approval from Iran, and NYT examined how South Korea's Sinokor has come to dominate roughly half of all tanker transits through the strait.

stories.headline: OPEC+ set to hold oil quotas steady for December
stories.summary: Delegates say major OPEC+ producers plan to keep output quotas unchanged next month even as ongoing Middle East conflict continues to disrupt crude supply.

stories.headline: Germany misses gas storage target as cold snap arrives
stories.summary: Germany is falling short of its official natural gas storage-filling target just as a cold snap hits, leaving the country with a thinner buffer against winter demand spikes.

stories.headline: Russia's shadow fleet improvises armor as Ukraine targets oil exports
stories.summary: Tankers in Russia's sanctions-evading shadow fleet are rigging makeshift drone defenses as Ukraine intensifies attacks on oil exports that help finance Moscow's war effort.

stories.headline: Xcel Energy unveils $70B renewables-heavy capital plan
stories.summary: Xcel Energy announced a five-year, $70 billion capital plan built around 9.2 GW of new renewables and 2.3 GW of storage, with CEO Bob Frenzel saying the utility can grow to meet demand while still protecting the environment.

stories.headline: Edison International warns of "dire" costs from stalled California wildfire reform
stories.summary: Edison International CEO Pedro Pizarro said delaying wildfire liability reform into 2027 will have significant and costly consequences for California ratepayers and utilities even as he expects policymakers to eventually act.

stories.headline: Hitachi's nuclear revenue climbs as SMR delivery date nears
stories.summary: Hitachi executives reported rising nuclear-segment revenue ahead of a key small modular reactor delivery, though they flagged inflation and long delivery timelines as risks to watch.

stories.headline: Nuclear fuel startup General Matter clears key NRC milestone
stories.summary: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission accepted an application from Peter Thiel-backed startup General Matter, clearing a path for construction to begin at a Department of Energy-owned site as the US seeks alternatives to Russian-sourced reactor fuel.

Energy.gaps: Latitude Media could not be searched directly and had no feed items, so no coverage could be confirmed. Canary Media, E&E News, and Argus Media were searched but no stories from the last 24-48 hours could be verified; the most recent dated items found (e.g., Canary Media's Oct. 26 newsletter) fell outside the window.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from the Chinese Communist Party's fifth plenum, especially the surprise Politburo promotion of anti-corruption czar Zhang Shengmin amid a historic purge of PLA generals, alongside fresh signs of economic strain (a weak October PMI and a sell-off prompting a stock-market rescue meeting). Business outlets are also tracking a wave of October EV delivery data and a landmark Alibaba-Apple AI partnership, while state media push official framing of plenum 'continuity' and diplomatic wins.

stories.headline: Zhang Shengmin promoted to Politburo as PLA purge empties military's top ranks
stories.summary: The Communist Party elevated anti-corruption chief Zhang Shengmin to the Politburo at its fifth plenum, the first mid-term Politburo addition in decades, after a purge left him as the only general alongside Xi on the Central Military Commission.

stories.headline: China's central bank and securities regulator to meet on stock market support
stories.summary: The PBOC, financial regulators and major banks are set to meet Monday to discuss expanding a relending facility for share buybacks after mainland stocks suffered their worst monthly decline in over a decade in October.

stories.headline: China's factory activity slips back into contraction in October
stories.summary: Official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1, with Xinhua attributing the dip to demand pulled forward before the National Day holiday, even as high-tech and equipment manufacturing kept expanding; WSJ separately reported broader economic activity losing steam sharply.

stories.headline: Chinese EV makers post divergent October results as price war bites
stories.summary: BYD sold 490,168 NEVs for a sixth straight month of growth and Xpeng topped 50,000 deliveries for the first time, while Nio, GWM and Huawei's HIMA brand posted sharp year-on-year declines.

stories.headline: Alibaba's Qwen to power Apple Intelligence in China
stories.summary: Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said the Qwen model will become the system-level AI backbone for Apple Intelligence in the Chinese market, which an industry expert called the first such deal for a top global hardware maker with a domestic Chinese model.

stories.headline: G20 foreign ministers meeting ends without joint communique
stories.summary: The Atlanta meeting chaired by Marco Rubio broke up without consensus amid splits over Ukraine, the US-Iran standoff and tariffs; China's vice foreign minister Ma Zhaoxu used the forum to promote Beijing's Global Security Initiative.

stories.headline: DeepSeek pushes into autonomous AI agents as coding race with OpenAI heats up
stories.summary: DeepSeek previewed a more autonomous 'super agent' capable of handling multiple tasks with minimal human input, intensifying competition with OpenAI and Anthropic; separately its Harness team open-sourced a bug-fixing agent prototype.

stories.headline: Chinese state TV skips first La Liga broadcast since Mbappe controversy
stories.summary: Chinese state broadcasters did not air Saturday's La Liga matches, the first since Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe sparked anger in China with a joke about Mao.

China.gaps: No recent China-specific items were found via search for Nikkei Asia, The Wire China, Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, Yicai Global, TechNode or ChinaTalk; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and The Economist block search so only feed items (where provided) were used for them.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by the deepening US-Iran standoff — stalled diplomacy, a new tanker attack near the Strait of Hormuz, and warnings from the IMF about the economic toll of the war — alongside Israel's unresolved coalition crisis after last week's election. Business titles are focused on quantifying the war's economic damage to Gulf economies alongside a steady drumbeat of UAE corporate and energy news.

stories.headline: US-Iran diplomacy falters as both sides trade threats ahead of new deadline
stories.summary: Middle East Eye reports Tehran is dismissing any diplomatic breakthrough with Washington even as Qatari-mediated talks continue in Doha, while Trump has said the US still has one or two targets left in Iran and could strike again within minutes. Iranian officials, including a senior lawmaker, have warned of a 'harsher reply than before' if threatened further.

stories.headline: Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck by unidentified objects in the Gulf
stories.summary: A Qatar Gas Transport Company LNG carrier was hit while transiting the Gulf near the Strait of Hormuz, with the company saying there were no injuries or environmental damage; Bloomberg separately reported Pakistan had negotiated Iranian approval for the vessel's safe passage beforehand. It is the latest in a long run of tanker incidents around Hormuz since the US-Iran war began.

stories.headline: Herzog opens coalition consultations as Arab parties back Eisenkot for PM
stories.summary: President Isaac Herzog called on Israeli party leaders to show flexibility and accept the election results as he prepares to begin formal coalition consultations, warning that entrenchment could force a repeat election. The Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot for prime minister, though both his bloc and Netanyahu's remain short of a 61-seat majority.

stories.headline: IMF: Gulf facing its 'largest oil shock in history' from Iran war
stories.summary: The IMF says the US-Israeli war with Iran has hit Gulf states harder than the rest of the region and forecasts the GCC economy will contract 4.8% in 2026, with oil output down 14%, a steeper drop than during the pandemic. Kuwait and Qatar are seen as most exposed given limited ability to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, while Saudi Arabia and the UAE have fared better thanks to alternative export routes.

stories.headline: WSJ investigation details billions in damage to US bases from Iranian strikes
stories.summary: A Wall Street Journal investigation using satellite imagery and a custom-built analysis tool found damage at more than two dozen US installations, offering the fullest public accounting yet of the toll from Iran's retaliatory strikes despite a US information blackout.

stories.headline: OPEC+ expected to hold output quotas steady for December
stories.summary: Delegates say major OPEC+ producers plan to keep production quotas unchanged for December as the Middle East conflict continues to curb supply, with oil prices also rising on fresh tanker attacks and Black Sea tensions.

stories.headline: DEWA deepens global push with Shanghai Electric tie-up
stories.summary: Dubai Electricity and Water Authority has signed a new agreement with China's Shanghai Electric as part of its continuing push to expand its utilities and energy business beyond the UAE.

stories.headline: Syria and Lebanon 'turning the corner' to rebuild, says US envoy
stories.summary: A US envoy says Syria and Lebanon are beginning to move past years of conflict toward reconstruction, as Lebanon separately pressed ahead with charges against Hezbollah members over an explosive shipment amid efforts to curb Iranian influence.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not find distinct recent lead stories from Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, The New Arab, Ynetnews, or Iran International via search. Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, WSJ, The Economist and BBC block search, so coverage from them is limited to the feed items provided.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage over the past 24-48 hours centers on the Democratic Republic of Congo's deepening crisis (Ebola toll and Tshisekedi's outreach to Putin), violence in Ethiopia, South Africa's upcoming local elections, and a cluster of African fintech/economy stories out of a Lagos tech conference and new Madagascar investment plans. Africanews and TechCabal dominate the fast-moving feed, while The Africa Report provides deeper political and business features.

stories.headline: Ebola deaths top 5,000 as fear of continent-wide spread mounts
stories.summary: Deaths from the Ebola outbreak in Congo have surpassed 5,000 as the disease continues to spread and cases are now being recorded in other African countries, according to the latest government figures.

stories.headline: Tshisekedi seeks Putin's help against Rwanda-backed rebels
stories.summary: DRC President Felix Tshisekedi said he wants Russia's involvement as a UN Security Council member in seeking peace with Rwanda, during talks with Vladimir Putin, as Kinshasa's eastern conflict escalates.

stories.headline: Drone strikes in Ethiopia kill at least 25: witnesses
stories.summary: Multiple drone strikes hit northern Ethiopia since Thursday, killing at least 25 civilians including children, according to witnesses and a medical source.

stories.headline: South Africa elections: Zille, Zuma and the battle for the big cities
stories.summary: South Africa's upcoming local elections could reshape the political map as the ANC fights to hold power, the DA pushes into new territory, and Jacob Zuma's MK party shakes up KwaZulu-Natal.

stories.headline: Gemcorp joins Madagascar to raise $5bn for energy, mining
stories.summary: Madagascar is partnering with asset manager Gemcorp Capital Management in a bid to raise as much as $5 billion to fund energy, infrastructure and mining projects on the island, per a Bloomberg report carried by Mining Weekly.

stories.headline: Youth Olympics open in Senegal, first Olympic event in Africa
stories.summary: The Youth Olympic Games opened in Dakar, marking the first time an Olympic event has been held on the African continent, as organizers hope it boosts Africa's role in global sport.

stories.headline: Verve plans phone tap-to-pay and AI agent payments
stories.summary: Payments company Verve's CEO said it plans to let customers tap their phones to pay and eventually allow AI assistants to make payments on users' behalf, part of a wave of African fintech announcements from a Lagos tech event.

stories.headline: A year after the coup, authoritarianism dashes Gen Z hopes in Madagascar
stories.summary: A year after Colonel Michael Randrianirina's military coup, Madagascar has not achieved the political refoundation he promised, leaving youth-led protest movements disillusioned.

Africa.gaps: Africa Confidential, The Continent and African Business returned only older archived content (weeks to months old) rather than anything from the last 24-48 hours. Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block direct search and had no relevant items in the provided feed, so their current Africa coverage could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Media trade outlets are converging on the deepening financial squeeze from AI on publishers, continued local-news contraction at traditional broadcasters, and fallout from Trump-era press-freedom legal battles. Entertainment trades (TheWrap, Variety, Deadline, THR) are dominated by Halloween-weekend SNL and awards-season content rather than industry-structure news.

stories.headline: Scripps cuts anchors, adds reporters in local TV overhaul
stories.summary: E.W. Scripps CEO Adam Symson announced a second wave of layoffs eliminating 431 positions as the company restructures local news around fewer on-air anchors and more field reporters, a move Poynter frames as a possible template for the future of local TV.

stories.headline: Publishers tell court AI content retrieval is already hurting their revenue
stories.summary: Digital Content Next testimony cited in court indicates member publishers are already seeing a revenue downturn following the arrival of AI search and retrieval tools, adding to mounting industry evidence of AI's toll on traffic and income.

stories.headline: Trump's $10 billion WSJ/Murdoch defamation suit dismissed with prejudice
stories.summary: A federal judge dismissed President Trump's lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch over the paper's reporting on his alleged birthday message to Jeffrey Epstein, ending the legal fight with prejudice.

stories.headline: Political ad spending surge keeps broadcast TV stations flush ahead of midterms
stories.summary: Even as advertisers shift dollars elsewhere, local broadcast stations are cashing in on a midterm-election advertising bonanza, with Texas races a prime example of the windfall.

stories.headline: How the Journal pierced a U.S. blackout on Iran base damage
stories.summary: The Journal detailed the investigative methodology behind its reporting on damage to U.S. bases, describing how reporters used satellite imagery, Iranian state media statements and custom software to get around an official information blackout.

stories.headline: Woodward's decision to unmask sources in new memoir sparks ethics debate
stories.summary: Status reports that Bob Woodward's choice to name previously confidential sources in his forthcoming memoir has set off a debate among journalists over whether anonymity promises should extend after a source's death.

stories.headline: Meta delays rollout of new commercial terms after publisher pushback
stories.summary: Digiday reports that Meta's proposed updated commercial terms over use of publisher content triggered a coordinated industry pushback, prompting the company to delay the rollout.

stories.headline: Paula Reid joins MS NOW as chief White House reporter amid press-access fight
stories.summary: Adweek notes the hire comes as CNN, MS NOW and Politico continue to press their joint lawsuit over White House press-pool access.

Media.gaps: No distinct, current (last 24-48h) media-industry story could be confirmed from Puck, FT, Bloomberg or The Guardian; available Guardian and Bloomberg items in the feed were outside the media-industry topic, and FT and Guardian block search so only feed items could be used.
